sentences.text: The Independent Commission Against Corruption compared chief executives’ survey responses from 2001 and 2007 to assess changes in corruption risks and prevention across the NSW public sector.
sentences.support:
their responses 
were compared with responses to similar surveys that 
had been sent to NSW public sector CEOs in 2001.

sentences.text: The comparison covered 165 organisations, excluding local councils, county councils and local Aboriginal land councils because they were outside the earlier survey.
sentences.support:
Local councils, 
county councils and local Aboriginal land councils are 
not included in this comparison subsample

sentences.text: ICAC concluded that perceived corruption risks had remained broadly stable while organisations reported adopting more prevention strategies, suggesting improved risk management.
sentences.support:
Together, these findings may indicate that the corruption 
risk management of the NSW public sector as a whole 
has improved.

sentences.text: ICAC advised organisations to review their prevention strategies for areas needing further controls.
sentences.support:
Organisations should, however, examine their own 
usage of corruption prevention strategies to identify any 
areas where further strategies are warranted.

findings.quote:
In conclusion, the corruption risk management of the 
NSW public sector as a whole appears to have improved 
since 2001.

Organisations should, however, examine their own 
usage of corruption prevention strategies to identify any 
areas where further strategies are warranted.

notes: Survey comparisons concern reported practices and perceived risks; no numbered recommendations list.
